title:
A joined DFE is made up of multiple other analytic outputs, but all of the same base type
(and usually not DFEs); This introduces a slightly different dependency in that the joined DFE is dependent on all
analytics which produce results of that output type (or a sub-type).
All the relevant source analytics must run (although they need not produce a result)
before the joined DFE is satisfied.

Analytic results can form the input to later analytics. In example below, if there are thirteen individual analytics in
an Revpro application , these produce several different sub-types of AnalyticResult.

Then, another (meta) analytic can be run to join these individual results to produce a summary result.  We want to
join the result of the individual analytics to produce a higher-level analytic result (which also features as
an important object in UI application).

This is done using a joined DFE that declares it takes an array of the results produced by the individual analytics.
This implicitly creates a dependency between the second-tier analytic and the various first-tier analytics.
Joined DFEs mix in the special marker type JoinedDataFlowEvent which declares the first-level analytic result type to be joined.

```
  entity type RevProAnalyticResult mixes AnalyticResult {
     (common fields)

  type ConsumptionOnInactiveMeterRevProAnalyticResult extends RevProAnalyticResult {
    (specific fields for "consumption on inactive meter")

  type ConsumptionOnInactiveMeterRevProAnalytic extends Analytic<MeterMonthHourlyElectricConsumption,ConsumptionOnInactiveMeterRevProAnalyticResult> {
    category : ~ = "RevPro"

  type AnotherRevProAnalyticResult ...
  type AnotherRevProAnalytic ...

  @dfe(...)
  type RevProAnalyticSet mixes JoinedDataFlowEvent<Location,RevProAnalyticResult>

  type RevenueOpportunity mixes Alert {
    (opportunity fields)

  type RevenueOpportunityCalculator mixes Analytic<RevProAnalyticSet, RevenueOpportunity> {
    category : ~ = "RevPro"
```
